thread:
Maria: Heads-up — we're planning the switch from project-scoped API keys to a claim-first service-account binding model. want to discuss console UX + telemetry for the rollout. 
Derek: +1. do we have a clear migration signal? how will routing decide between legacy keys and claims? :thinking_face: 
Shreya: TL;DR: plan is phased. phase 1 = opt-in claim sync in console (admins enable per-org). phase 2 = warn-only for legacy keys. phase 3 = enforce. need metrics for user impact.
Jonathan: Important: routing policy must prefer exact route bindings over org-wide claims. otherwise we risk surprising quota changes.
Maria: Agreed. propose routing priority: 1) explicit route-binding (service-account->route), 2) project-claim, 3) org-claim, 4) legacy-key fallback.
Derek: That ordering makes sense. for fallback we should add a circuit-breaker when rates jump 10x. ops-bot can we add alert on token_routing_fallback rate?
ops-bot: noted. I'll emit metric token.routing.fallback{reason:legacy,org,project} and an alert when count > 100/min for 5m.
Shreya: We also need to tag every token with token_origin + token_claim_id so telemetry can split cost/latency by origin during rollout.
Jonathan: UI idea: in console, show a "binding preview" when you toggle claim-sync that lists effective routes and quotas per SA. e.g.,
```
Binding preview:
- SA: billing-service@acme
- Bound routes: api.generate, api.embed
- Quota scope: project:5432 (50k/mo)
- Impersonation TTL: 15m
- Notes: legacy keys still accepted until May 1
```
Derek: Implementation detail: claim-sync will create ephemeral routing-claims in the control-plane DB. each claim must store: claim_id, sa_id, routes[], ttl, created_by. we should audit-write when created/removed.
Maria: Right. add an audit event token.claim.sync.created and token.claim.sync.removed. Also surface in event feed for SRE.
Shreya: Security question: who can enable claim-sync? org-admin only? or project-admin? my vote = org-admin with an override checkbox for projects. reduces blast radius.
Jonathan: agree org-admin default. project-admin override is acceptable with explicit justification + audit. we should require MFA for enabling in prod orgs.
Derek: one more edge: what if a SA is bound to multiple projects with different quotas? routing needs to attach quota labels and reject if request would exceed project quota. add a preflight that returns 429 with structured reason.
Maria: Good call. Let's standardize error payload: {"code":"QuotaExceeded","scope":"project:5432","available":0,"recommended":0} in v2 API.
Shreya: Also include helpful console link in error (short link) so devs can see binding + quota in console. reduces support churn.
deploy-bot: FYI deploying claim-sync feature flag to staging at 10:30am PT. rollout=canary(5%)->50%->100% over 48h if no errors.
Derek: For telemetry, instrument: token_origin, claim_id, routing_path, decision_latency_ms, fallback_reason. aggregate per-minute, per-route, per-org.
Maria: We'll add a regression alert if decision_latency_ms p50 > 20ms or p99 > 200ms after canary.
Jonathan: Minor UI nit: show a delta view comparing legacy key behaviour vs claim-bound behaviour in the console before enabling — helps product managers decide.
Shreya: I'll mock one in Figma and drop link. also prepping a one-pager for support.
Maria: Next steps: Shreya mock, Derek implement metrics + audit events, Jonathan update routing priority logic, ops-bot add alerts, deploy-bot handle flag rollouts. I'll schedule an 30-min sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Derek: cool. tagging @jonathan for routing PR review when ready.
Jonathan: will review. thanks all.
ops-bot: alert created: token.routing.fallback.rate > 100/min (5m window).
Maria: End — saving this thread for runbook reference.
